messages.subject: correlating sets of residuals?
parts:
Hello lavaan users!
 
I'm very new to lavaan and have been able to practice fitting models both in EQS, Mplus and lavaan to make sure I'm doing things correctly. There is a functionality in EQS and Mplus that I find very convenient but have not been able to uncover it in lavaan.
 
For example, in EQS It is possible to correlate sets of residual variances by setting:
 
/COVARIANCES
E1 to E5 = *;
 
And that correlates all the residual variances for observed indicators 1 to 5.
 
In lavaan so far I have been getting along just fine going variable-per-variable in a pairwise fashion, but this is going to become quite cumebrsome as soon as I have a large dataset. I'm sure there is an argument of some function somewhere that I am not finding. I would very much appreciate to be pointed in the right direction here.
 
Thank you all!
 
- Elia.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: correlating sets of residuals?
parts:
I know you can do a "correlate everything" approach because you can put multiple variables on both sides of an operator:
  • E1 + E2 + E3 + E4 + E5 ~~ E1 + E2 + E3 + E4 + E5
But I'm not sure there's a pairwise operator like Mplus has, if you just wanted to correlate residuals (e.g.) for the same indicators measured at multiple occasions:
  • v1_time1 v2_time1 v3_time1 PWITH v1_time2 v2_time2 v3_time2
That would be a very convenient operator, but I don't think it exists in lavaan yet.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: correlating sets of residuals?
parts:
On 09/15/2013 06:49 PM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
> I know you can do a "correlate everything" approach because you can put
> multiple variables on both sides of an operator:
>

> * E1 + E2 + E3 + E4 + E5 ~~ E1 + E2 + E3 + E4 + E5

This will not work, since you will have duplicated elements (E1 ~~ E2
and E2 ~~ E1), and lavaanify() will spit out an error.

> But I'm not sure there's a pairwise operator like Mplus has, if you just
> wanted to correlate residuals (e.g.) for the same indicators measured at
> multiple occasions:
>
> * v1_time1 v2_time1 v3_time1 PWITH v1_time2 v2_time2 v3_time2

>
> That would be a very convenient operator, but I don't think it exists in
> lavaan yet.

Correct.

I see two possible approaches here:

a) a dedicated 'pairwise' correlation operator (a la PWITH); perhaps
something like "~p~"

b) an additional auto.* flag; perhaps something like auto.cov.ind (we
already have auto.cov.y, but this excludes indicators)

Yves.
